subject.title: [Feature]: Disable image optimization when images are uploaded to Slack

question: Should Slack uploads preserve original image bytes by default, expose an explicit opt-out or per-call fidelity control, or keep the current shared image-optimization policy?
rationale: The source path is clear, but the fix adds or changes public channel behavior/config and can affect successful compressed uploads versus raw oversize failures, so maintainers need to choose the contract before implementation.

options.title: Add Explicit Fidelity Control
options.body: Add a documented default-off Slack upload-fidelity control or per-call flag that disables image optimization for intended raw uploads while preserving current defaults.

options.title: Make Raw Upload Default
options.body: Change Slack uploads to preserve original bytes whenever they fit the configured cap, accepting the compatibility risk that some currently optimized sends may fail instead of compressing.

options.title: Keep Current Policy
options.body: Document that Slack uploads use the shared media pipeline and require explicit direct-upload instructions or future force-document work for pristine file transfer.

recommendation.title: Add Explicit Fidelity Control
recommendation.body: Add a documented default-off Slack upload-fidelity control or per-call flag that disables image optimization for intended raw uploads while preserving current defaults.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans shared media policy, Slack channel behavior, and config compatibility, and this person has the strongest sampled history on the shared boundary.
